 Gujarat Weather Swings Sharply as Naliya Falls to 17°C
 By Harpreet Singh 
 November 10, 2026 
 0 
 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp 
 Gujarat is experiencing a sharp temperature swing, with north-easterly winds bringing cooler mornings and evenings while daytime temperatures are expected to rise to as high as 38°C across parts of the state, according to a report citing the latest weather data from the India Meteorological Department.
 Naliya in Kutch recorded the state’s lowest minimum temperature at 17°C, making it the coolest reported location in Gujarat. The fall in nighttime temperatures has brought noticeable morning and evening chill in the Kutch region, while strong sunlight is pushing temperatures higher through the afternoon.
 The weather pattern is being driven by dry and relatively cool winds from the north and north-east. These winds have lowered minimum temperatures in several areas, creating conditions that feel cooler early in the day before the heat rises rapidly after sunrise.
 The report describes the pattern as a mixed season, with residents experiencing a combination of winter-like mornings and summer-like afternoons. In many parts of Gujarat, the maximum temperature is expected to remain around 38°C, increasing discomfort during the middle of the day despite the cooler start.
 The wide gap between daytime and nighttime temperatures is also affecting how residents plan daily activities. People commuting, working outdoors or travelling early in the morning may experience markedly different conditions by afternoon. The report says the difference between day and night temperatures could be close to 20°C in some areas.
 Such rapid changes can also complicate routine health precautions. The report links the mixed conditions with the possibility of a rise in cases of cold, cough, fever and viral infections, although it does not provide confirmed case numbers or a separate health department advisory. Residents may therefore encounter cooler air during morning travel and stronger heat during afternoon movement within the same day.
 For cities such as Ahmedabad, the changing pattern is relevant to commuting, construction work, street vending and other activities exposed to outdoor conditions. However, the supplied report does not provide a separate Ahmedabad minimum or maximum temperature, nor does it identify any city-level restrictions or municipal response.
 The immediate forecast remains defined by the contrast between cooler mornings and hotter afternoons. Temperatures in Naliya and other parts of Gujarat will continue to be watched as the north-easterly wind pattern develops and the state moves through this period of pronounced day-night variation.
